name: Stones Throw Records
ownershipStory: Chris Manak, a Bay Area DJ and producer known as Peanut Butter Wolf, started Stones Throw in 1996 to release the recordings he had made with his rap partner Charizma (Charles Hicks), who was shot and killed in a 1993 carjacking at age 20. The label grew into a home for producer-led, crate-dug hip-hop built around total creative control: Madlib's Lootpack and his own sprawling catalogue, and, in 2004, Madvillainy, a pairing of Madlib with MF DOOM that Manak proposed himself by phone, then hosted at his own house. It went on to release J Dilla's Donuts in 2006.
hook: A label built to release one dead friend's tape that became the place producers went for total creative control.

blurb.age13: Chris Manak, known as Peanut Butter Wolf, started Stones Throw Records in 1996 to put out music he had made with his friend and rap partner Charizma, who had been killed a few years earlier. The label grew into a home for sample-based hip-hop producers who wanted room to make strange, personal records, including Madlib, MF DOOM, and J Dilla.
blurb.adult: Stones Throw's mark on this map is less any single release than the kind of control it gave producers over their own work. Founder Chris Manak has said in interviews that he personally proposed pairing his own artist Madlib with MF DOOM, a call that became Madvillainy (2004), and that Stones Throw hosted the recording sessions at his house, Madlib building beats in the basement while DOOM wrote upstairs.
